headline: Shakib Al Hasan says he is ready to return home and face trial if given security
summary: The former Bangladesh captain and Awami League ally says he is willing to face murder and corruption charges in court if the government guarantees his safety.
details: Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan has expressed his readiness to return from a two-year exile in the United States and face trial on charges including murder and corruption.
Speaking to Reuters from Sri Lanka, the 39-year-old cricketer stated that he is happy to go back and face the court trial if the government ensures his security.
Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, has been living abroad since the government of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was toppled in August 2024.
He currently faces two active cases: one involving the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another regarding alleged corruption.
Shakib dismissed the murder case as 'laughable,' claiming it was filed on a day he was playing a match in Toronto, Canada.
The cricketer also revealed that a previous attempt to return home in late 2024 collapsed after he was told mid-journey to turn back while in an airport lounge.
He further stated that he would not consider distancing himself from Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League as a condition for his return.
Beyond legal battles, Shakib hopes to play a farewell series at home and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 one-day World Cup before retiring.
He mentioned that his bank accounts have been frozen for a year and a half pending investigation.

Speaking to Reuters from Sri Lanka, the 39-year-old cricketer stated that he is happy to go back and face the court trial if the government ensures his security.

Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, has been living abroad since the government of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was toppled in August 2024.

He currently faces two active cases: one involving the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another regarding alleged corruption.

Shakib dismissed the murder case as 'laughable,' claiming it was filed on a day he was playing a match in Toronto, Canada.

The cricketer also revealed that a previous attempt to return home in late 2024 collapsed after he was told mid-journey to turn back while in an airport lounge.

He further stated that he would not consider distancing himself from Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League as a condition for his return.

Beyond legal battles, Shakib hopes to play a farewell series at home and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 one-day World Cup before retiring.

He mentioned that his bank accounts have been frozen for a year and a half pending investigation.

headline: 9 killed in two-bus collision in Sylhet
summary: A head-on crash between a Unique Paribahan and a Bengal Paribahan bus on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway left 9 people dead.
details: At least 9 people were killed in a head-on collision between two buses in Sylhet’s Osmaninagar on Friday morning.
The accident occurred around 7:00 am in the Kashikapon area on the Dhaka-Sylhet highway.
A Unique Paribahan bus and a Bengal Paribahan bus collided head-on, killing seven people on the spot.
Several others were injured in the crash and were rushed to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital.
One more victim died at the hospital, bringing the total death toll to 9 according to some reports, while others cite 8.
Police are currently working to identify the victims of the tragedy.
